text: Sofia starts a weekly working group to think about strategies on how to spread the word about this local POCAS, so that they can get more people to come join and help and support the group, especially under the current oppressive government. They also spend some time on the ground, knocking on people's doors, spreading the word.
scenario:
Title: Tenuous Balance

The city hums with an uneasy rhythm. Surveillance drones buzz overhead while the streets below bustle with markets and protests in a delicate dance. Mutual aid groups keep spirits high but tensions linger on street corners, as militias patrol alongside police. The air remains hazy from smog and heatwaves, reminding residents of the looming environmental threats that could tip their precarious balance.

On a typical day, people navigate through checkpoints and permits, juggling multiple currencies for rent and groceries. The mega-corporations loom like shadows, but co-ops and solidarity networks still thrive in neighborhoods across Mexico City. Life goes on with an undercurrent of anxiety, as residents hold their breaths, hoping the tenuous equilibrium doesn't tip into disaster.

The streets tell a complex story—of resilience amidst conflict, of adaptation amid environmental challenges, and of a capitalist system that both sustains and threatens. It's a city where hope and despair walk hand in hand, where progress and regression are constant companions on the journey towards an uncertain future.

text: Start community kitchen, getting some equipment from neighbours, people can order meals and some set menus with one or two dishes. It's hyperlocal and nutritious. Pablo will help running errands picking equipments and food up. Since we are good at chaordination. We will be doing a bit of dumpster diving and getting scraps from markets. We will start growing micro-greens and herbs.

text: Start "Taller El Tuercas". A workshop for furniture repair and creation. Here we repair anything that breaks; we specialize in furniture, but we’re also thinking of opening a vehicle workshop that we’re currently developing. You can come with anything you want to repair, and we’ll teach you and lend you tools in exchange for something else you produce.

text: Expand the community kitchen project with some in-house oyster mushroom growing. We have developed a better system mapping places for dumpster diving and market scraps gathering. jHammza and the "El Tuercas" workshop will support the efforts with a couple of retrofitted cargo bicycle for food delivery and resource collection.
scenario:
In the first month of Phase 1, the POCAS space has seen incremental progress across its various protocolitos. Sofia's weekly working group focused on outreach and recruitment has begun raising awareness among nearby residents about their community initiatives. However, sustainable growth remains uncertain due to limited reserves and minimal shared infrastructure.

The community kitchen protocolito is off to a promising start, with participants coordinating resources and skills to provide nutritious meals while also strengthening local networks. Rok's coordination abilities and Pablo's determination will be key in managing the workload.

"Taller El Tuercas" workshop has shown potential for skill-sharing and repairing items, but Sofia and jHammza may struggle to dedicate enough time given their other commitments. Both furniture repair and vehicle workshops could see limited progress over this phase.

The research project on drone jamming systems is ambitious considering the lack of tools and expertise within the POCAS space. Laura, Pablo, and Sofia are motivated but their skills are not well-aligned with the complexity of building a functional system. They may focus more on research and fundraising efforts rather than actual prototyping in this initial phase.

text: For the drone jamming research the three of us will look for someone in the community who can help us further develop and prototype our defensive weapon.

text: From Taller "El Tuercas". With the advances made on the first prototype vehicle donated to the community kitchen, we’ve discovered that food that spoils along the way can be used as fuel. This fuel can make the vehicle move much faster; however, this technology is also dangerous for anyone who doesn’t know how to handle it, and it could even be developed into weaponry.
